evidenceAudit.scope: Recognition and treatment of psychosis and schizophrenia in India at primary, district and tertiary level: diagnosis, organic exclusion, risperidone initiation, switching, clozapine for treatment resistance, management of agitation, suicide and violence, metabolic monitoring, duration and referral, built on the ICMR Psychosis STW (October 2019) and the Indian Psychiatric Society schizophrenia guideline (2017).
findings: Diagnostic features, red flags and referral levels, organic work-up, risperidone 2 mg at bedtime then 3–4 mg (range 2–8 mg/day), trihexyphenidyl 2 mg (2–6 mg/day), 6–8 week adequate trial, switching and clozapine after two failed antipsychotics, ECT indications, side-effect schedule and treatment duration checked against the ICMR Psychosis STW (October 2019).

Olanzapine 10–30 mg/day, haloperidol 5–20 mg/day, aripiprazole 10–30 mg/day, clozapine 150–600 mg/day (maximum 900), depot preparations, metabolic monitoring (baseline, 6 weeks, 12 weeks, annually) and maintenance duration checked against IPS CPG 2017 (Table 5, Table 6, Table 19).
Haloperidol 10 mg with promethazine 50 mg IM and olanzapine 10 mg IM for acute agitation from the BestBETs review (TREC-India trial).
Clozapine titration and ANC monitoring from the US prescribing information.
unverifiedSections: The ICMR STW Table 1 dosing was not in the opened text; olanzapine, haloperidol, aripiprazole and clozapine ranges come from IPS 2017.
Lorazepam is named for agitation by IPS 2017 but no dose was found in the opened sources.
First-episode maintenance: ICMR gives about 2 years; IPS gives 1–2 years. Both are shown.
ANC thresholds are from the US label; Indian practice may differ.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Psychosis is loss of contact with reality — hallucinations, delusions and disorganised behaviour — and schizophrenia is its commonest chronic form. In India most patients first present to families, faith healers or primary care. The ICMR workflow asks primary care to suspect psychosis (talking or laughing to self, suspiciousness, poor self-care, decline in function), exclude organic causes and substance use, assess risk to self and others, start risperidone with trihexyphenidyl if needed, and refer when diagnosis is unclear, risk is high, response is poor or special situations (pregnancy, comorbidity) exist. Treatment is long term; clozapine is used after two adequate failed trials.
keyMechanisms: Excess mesolimbic dopamine activity is linked to positive symptoms.
Antipsychotics block dopamine D2 receptors; blockade in the nigrostriatal pathway causes extrapyramidal symptoms.
Second-generation antipsychotics also block serotonin 5-HT2A and cause more metabolic effects.
Clozapine is effective in treatment resistance but causes neutropenia, myocarditis and seizures.

symptoms: Hearing voices; talking, smiling or laughing to self (ICMR STW)
Suspiciousness and fear without obvious reason (delusions) (ICMR STW)
Withdrawal, poor self-care, decline in work or study (ICMR STW)
physicalSigns: Signs of organic disease (fever, focal deficits, confusion)
redFlags: Immediate threat to self or others: refer (ICMR STW)
Diagnostic confusion or suspected organic condition (ICMR STW)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Temporal link to cannabis, stimulants or withdrawal; urine toxicology.
Neurological signs, late onset; neuroimaging (ICMR STW).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Hallucinations, delusions, disorganised behaviour with social and occupational dysfunction.
Highest tolerated dose for 6–8 weeks (clozapine 3–6 months).
Failure of two adequate antipsychotic trials, one second generation.
Catatonia, suicidal risk, severe violence, refusal to eat, clozapine resistance.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Hallucinations, delusions; focal signs suggest organic cause
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Thorough examination in diagnostic confusion (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Assess
actions: Look for hallucinations, delusions, disorganisation and decline (ICMR STW).
Assess risk to self and others; refer catatonia, high risk and diagnostic confusion to taluk or district level (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Start treatment
actions: Risperidone 2 mg at bedtime for 1 week, then 3–4 mg (ICMR STW).
Trihexyphenidyl 2 mg in the morning if extrapyramidal symptoms (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Review and switch
actions: Check sleepiness and EPS at 2 weeks; weight, menstrual and sexual effects at 1–2 months (ICMR STW).
Adequate dose for 6–8 weeks before switching (ICMR STW).
After 2 failed antipsychotics: clozapine (ICMR STW; IPS 2017).
Non-adherence: consider depot (ICMR STW; IPS 2017 Table 6).

clinicalManagement.title: Agitation, suicide and violence
actions: Rapid tranquillisation if needed (see medicines); monitor vital signs closely (BestBETs).
Suicidal risk, catatonia, refusal of food or severe violence: inpatient care; consider ECT (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Maintenance
actions: Stabilise about 6 months on the same dose, then reduce to minimum effective (ICMR STW).
First episode about 2 years (ICMR) or 1–2 years (IPS); multiple episodes indefinitely or 5 years or more (ICMR STW; IPS 2017).

teaching.scope: Psychosis and schizophrenia across Indian care levels.
learningObjectives: Recognise psychosis and exclude organic causes.
Know when to switch, use clozapine or refer.
keyPoints: Risperidone 2 mg at night, then 3–4 mg.
Give 6–8 weeks at an adequate dose before switching.
Clozapine after two failures, with ANC monitoring.
Monitor weight and fasting glucose at minimum.
